extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, researchers, and policymakers interested in patent law and AI-generated inventions
extracted.subtask_description: Academic legal research / dissertation analyzing how existing patent law applies to AI-generated inventions across jurisdictions, identifying challenges and recommending reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrinal analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctrinal analysis, which involves examining existing legal texts, statutes, case law, and authoritative legal commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use doctrinal methods to explore the current legal framework surrounding patent law with emphasis on treatment of AI-generated inventions; critically analyze national patent laws, international treaties, and relevant case law to assess their capacity to address challenges posed by AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the global nature of the issue, adopt a comparative legal methodology analyzing how various legal systems approach patentability of AI-generated inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare jurisdictions (explicitly names United States, European Union, India, China, Japan) to highlight similarities/differences, identify best practices and areas needing reform; focus on legislative approaches, regulatory frameworks, and key case law in each jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case study analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine case studies involving AI technology and patenting practices, including key case law and landmark decisions regarding patenting of inventions created by AI systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select representative cases (e.g., landmark U.S. and European decisions) to illustrate how courts and patent offices interpret existing laws in context of AI innovations; use outcomes and legal arguments from cases to identify practical implications and gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews with experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate semi-structured interviews with industry experts, legal practitioners, and policymakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct interviews with professionals in intellectual property law, AI technology, and patent law to gain practical perspectives on challenges and potential solutions; use qualitative insights to complement doctrinal and comparative findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical legal theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate critical legal theory to explore philosophical and ethical dimensions of patenting AI-generated inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use theoretical lens to examine implications of attributing inventorship or ownership to non-human entities; analyze whether such changes align with or challenge established legal norms and principles; consider moral questions about credit, creativity, and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary source research
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize secondary sources including academic articles, books, reports, and commentaries to gain broader understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ secondary literature for context, historical background, and current trends in patent law as it pertains to AI; integrate doctrinal materials with scholarly commentary to support arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrinal synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry out a doctrinal synthesis of gathered information to draw conclusions regarding adequacy of patent law for AI-generated inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize primary and secondary research, comparative findings, case studies, and interviews to propose recommendations for legal reform; aim to present clear, well-supported arguments about how patent law should evolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core patentability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental principles of patent law: novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze applicability of these traditional patent criteria to AI-generated inventions; assess whether and how concepts like novelty and inventive step can be meaningfully applied when an invention is autonomously produced by AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship and authorship issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine legal complexities surrounding inventorship, ownership, and authorship in context of AI as potential inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on defining inventorship, assigning ownership of AI-generated works, and questions of legal accountability; evaluate whether current doctrines accommodate non-human inventors and explore potential doctrinal or legislative adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and philosophical implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore moral questions and broader societal implications of granting patent rights to AI-generated inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess consequences for human creativity and innovation, consider whether AI can be considered an 'inventor' in traditional sense, and discuss implications for credit, accountability, and the purpose of intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying legal challenges and conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and discuss key legal challenges posed by AI-generated inventions and potential conflicts with traditional patent laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether existing legal frameworks can adequately address issues such as inventorship, ownership, and accountability; highlight tensions and examples where traditional doctrines may be incompatible with AI realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals for reform and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide proposals for legal reform including legislative amendments, regulatory reforms, and international cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base recommendations on combined doctrinal, comparative, case-study, and empirical insights; discuss policy options to balance protection of AI-generated inventions with broader goals of innovation, competition, and IP rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissertation structure as production guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the dissertation into distinct chapters each focusing on specific aspects of AI and patent law (e.g., introduction, evolution of AI, legal framework, comparative analysis, ethics, case studies, challenges, reform proposals, conclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chapter organization to ensure systematic coverage: introduce objectives/methodology, analyze historical/technical background, examine legal frameworks and jurisdictional contrasts, present case studies, discuss ethical dimensions, identify challenges, and conclude with reform proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of case-study subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus case studies on specific examples of AI-generated outputs (e.g., artworks, music, literary works) that have undergone patent or IP application processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete domains (art, music, literature, technical inventions) to illustrate how patent offices and courts have handled AI-generated works; analyze outcomes and legal reasoning in each domain to draw broader lessons.
